matches.rationale: GT 1 describes inflated performance claims in the abstract (2×–50×) that are not uniformly supported by experimental data. Pred 3 identifies that Section 4.2 overstates gains (claiming >50× for humanoid tasks when Table 1 shows only one task exceeds 50×), and Pred 6 notes Figure 1 caption inconsistency with the same issue. Both findings capture the same underlying problem of exaggerated performance ranges.

GT 2 concerns confusion about depth definition (total Dense layers vs. discrete depth levels 4, 8, 16, etc.) across sections. None of the findings address this architectural definition inconsistency; Pred 8 discusses critic output formulation (dot-product vs L2), which is a different methodological issue.

GT 3 criticizes lack of disclosure about training regime modifications (learning rates, compute budgets) for very deep networks. None of the findings identify missing protocol details or transparency issues regarding training hyperparameters at extreme depths.

GT 4 concerns overstated claims about qualitatively distinct emergent behaviors from depth scaling (Section 4.3) based on limited visualization evidence. None of the findings address this specific claim about behavioral emergence or the weakness of supporting evidence for qualitative skill changes.
GT 5 identifies a fabricated reference (Neumann and Gros, 2022) in Related Work. None of the findings check or report issues with citation validity or fabricated references.

GT 6 concerns omission of limitations discussion (compute costs, environmental impact) in the Conclusion. None of the findings identify missing ethical considerations or inadequate discussion of computational trade-offs and accessibility.

GT 7 criticizes inflated rhetorical language in the abstract ('unlock substantial improvements,' 'significantly boost'). None of the findings address rhetorical tone or presentation style issues; they focus on numeric and logical inconsistencies.

GT 8 describes modified/inflated data in Figure 6 showing consistently higher joint actor-critic scaling performance that misrepresents nuanced interactions. Pred 5 directly identifies that Figure 6's caption claims 30% average improvement from joint scaling, but the actual data yields only ~11.6%, exposing the same data integrity issue.

GT 9 identifies narrative inconsistency in Section 4.5 where text claims batch size scaling is effective with depth, but data shows inconsistent/minimal improvements. Pred 4 captures this exact contradiction between the subsection title/caption asserting batch size benefits and body text stating 'only marginal or inconsistent improvements.'

GT 10 concerns omission of ethical considerations (carbon footprint, reproducibility challenges) in Conclusion/Impact Statement. None of the findings address missing ethical disclosures or societal impact discussions.

GT 11 criticizes promotional/conclusive tone in Introduction ('unlocks the ability to scale... yielding performance improvements that surpass'). None of the findings identify rhetorical overstatement or presentation manipulation in the Introduction.

GT 12 identifies unrealistically large 983× improvement claim for Humanoid Big Maze in Table 1. Pred 11 directly addresses this, noting the improvement calculation (40/0.06 = 666.7×) doesn't match the reported 600×, exposing the same data integrity issue in that table entry.

GT 13 describes inconsistency between critic output defined as L2 distance in Preliminaries versus dot-product similarity used in experiments. Pred 8 identifies exactly this discrepancy: Section 3 defines dot-product while hyperparameter table and Figure 9 use L2 distance, capturing the same methodological inconsistency.

GT 14 concerns undisclosed MJX/Brax version discrepancies in Appendix B.2 affecting reproducibility. None of the findings identify this specific protocol transparency issue regarding environment simulation versions.

GT 15 criticizes overly broad attribution that CRL is critical for depth scaling, marginalizing mixed results from GCBC/GCSL. None of the findings address this claim interpretation issue about algorithm-specific benefits.

GT 16 identifies inconsistent wall-clock time scaling in appendix tables, particularly unusually low times for very deep models. Pred 7 directly captures this: Table 3 vs Table 4 show conflicting wall-clock times for Humanoid U-Maze Depth 64 (46.74h vs 17.33h), exposing the same data integrity issue.

GT 17 concerns overgeneralization of qualitative behavior claims in Conclusion based on limited humanoid visualizations. None of the findings identify this specific claim interpretation distortion about implicitly acquired skills or overstated behavioral improvements.
